intro: KSC.JUSNREM connects legal scholarship, institutional experience and technology to address how law is made, how public power is exercised and how institutions respond to change. Its publications and developing platforms bring together constitutional governance, legislative research, fiscal order and digital innovation, with practical applications for governments, institutions, businesses and researchers.
sections: Qanun Maps is being developed to make Pakistan’s legislation easier to find, read and understand in its constitutional and institutional context. It forms part of a wider programme connecting legal knowledge with the responsibilities and decisions of the institutions that apply it.

JUS.smart emerged from the Internet Governance Forum in 2024. Its continuing development encompasses the Sovereign Intelligence Engine, Sovereign Governance Engine and Sovereign Operating System, extending the programme’s focus towards the responsible use of intelligence in public institutions.

Khurram Chughtai works alongside his sons, Khyzar and Yazar, who support projects throughout KSC.JUSNREM. Their collaboration combines legal and institutional experience with database development, research and entrepreneurial initiative. Together, they founded Qanun Maps and contributed to its foundational work.

Advocate and founder of KSC.JUSNREM, Khurram brings more than two decades of legal practice to research and development at the intersection of law, technology and governance. His work provides the legal and institutional foundations for the ecosystem’s publications and developing platforms.

Khyzar contributes to database development and foundational work across the ecosystem. He studies Data Sciences and Economics at Lahore University of Management Sciences and is a co-founder of XINBIL, a digital assets ecosystem.
XINBIL’s Pakistan–Saudi Arabia Digital Asset Corridor project was showcased at the PIF Private Sector Forum in Riyadh in February 2026.

Yazar contributes to foundational development across KSC.JUSNREM’s projects. He studies Law and Mathematics through Cambridge International A Levels and serves as Head of the Entrepreneurship Society at ICAS, combining his academic interests with practical involvement in the programme.

JUS.novate, JUS.QBATE and ENVOVXN Intelligence form part of the wider development programme, alongside initiatives including XINBIL and Zimmadar. Each has a distinct focus, with its work and development stage presented separately.
Technical support for Qanun Maps has been contributed by HKA SMARTVXN.

Our purpose is to make legal intelligence useful in practice: legislation that people can understand, responsibilities that institutions can identify, and decisions grounded in evidence and lawful authority.
